raw_case_text:
The patient was a 65-year-old man, with a body mass index of 15.2 Kg/m2 and a smoking index of 800 (40 years x 20 cigarettes). In September 2021, the patient was admitted to the hospital for lung occupancy with enlarged lymph nodes in the right neck; a new biopsy of bronchial neoplasm in the lower lobe of the left lung led to the diagnosis of squamous carcinoma with liver metastasis and a biopsy of lymphatic tissue on the right neck as lymphoid hyperplasia with necrosis. The patient received four cycles of albumin paclitaxel combined with lobaplatin regimen chemotherapy and penpulimab immunotherapy from October to December 2021, and the lymph nodes on the right side of the neck shrank significantly. Treatment with cycles 5-7 of penpulimab was continued from January to February 2022. In mid-January 2022, the patient showed enlarged lymph nodes on the left side of the neck, and positron emission tomography-CT showed that the left lower lobe of the lung had increased density in the form of strips and mild fluorodeoxyglucose F 18 uptake. Considering that the tumor activity was suppressed after treatment, the systemic lymph nodes were enlarged, and fluorodeoxyglucose F 18 metabolism was active. A biopsy of the left cervical lymph node ruled out metastatic cancer, and in combination with immunohistochemistry, non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) was diagnosed in February 2022. Chemotherapy with the R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, hydroxydaunorubicin hydrochloride (doxorubicin hydrochloride), vincristine (Oncovin), and prednisone) regimen was administered on March 18, 2022, and cycle 8 penpulimab treatment was administered on March 23, 2022 ( Figure 1 ). On March 30, 2022, he developed a fever, with the highest body temperature being 39 C, cough, a small amount of white foamy sputum, and dyspnea; cefdinir and ibuprofen proved ineffective. On April 3, the patient was admitted to the Respiratory Department for persistent cough and dyspnea since Mar 30, 2022, and  Figure 2  shows the patient's CT. The patient's condition was diagnosed as severe pneumonia type I respiratory failure. Broad-spectrum antibiotics were administered, and the patient was transferred to the intensive care unit on April 9, 2022, for the treatment of worsening dyspnea, increased pulmonary infiltrates ( Figure 3 ), and poor oxygenation index.
At the time of admission to the intensive care unit, the patient had severe hypoxemia with an oxygen sum index of 131 and cellular immunodeficiency. Pathogenic test results were negative for galactomannan antigen test, TORCH, nine respiratory pathogens via nucleic acid tests, Pneumocystis pneumonia, blood cultures, and sputum cultures except for elevated serum -beta-D glucan of 199.32 pg/mL. The patient showed no distinct pathogenic evidence of a poor anti-infective effect. It is noteworthy that the patient was on penpulimab a week before the current onset, which is an ICI and has the potential to cause CIP. The patient's lung imaging showed progressive interstitial pneumonia with persistent fever, poor anti-infective effect, and a high systemic inflammatory response, which could not be explained by infection. Moreover, the use of rituximab in the R-CHOP regimen for lymphoma, where anti-CD20-mediated B-cell depletion has a synergistic effect with PD-1 blockers to promote cytotoxic T-lymphocyte activation, may have increased CIP risk. Therefore, the possibility of CIP was considered in the patient. Since CIP requires the exclusion of infection as well as other diseases, the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid was collected and sent for metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to exclude infection. Further, the patient tested negative for autoimmune-related antibodies, thus excluding interstitial lung changes due to autoimmune diseases.
The patient had a large lesion in the entire lung and severe respiratory failure. Considering that the patient was diagnosed as having CIP grade 4, methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg (ESMO guideline recommended dose) was administered based on empirical anti-infection. The patient had hypoxemia, with an SPO2 of 66% and a respiratory rate of 32 bpm, requiring further respiratory support; therefore, noninvasive mechanical ventilation was chosen as the initial respiratory support strategy. The patient was conscious and had good treatment compliance and airway self-purification; therefore, he was ventilated in the awake prone position during noninvasive ventilation, and his respiratory status was closely monitored during this period. After the above treatment, the patient's clinical symptoms resolved significantly on April 10, 2022, while the mNGS results showed no pathogenic microorganisms, thus ruling out severe pneumonia and allowing the discontinuation of antibiotics. Chest CT was repeated on April 11, 2022, for bilateral lung lesion absorption ( Figure 4 ). The patient was removed from the ventilator and transferred to the respiratory department on April 12, 2022. The methylprednisolone dose was reduced to 40 mg a day on April 15, 2022. Oxygen therapy was discontinued on April 20, 2022, and a repeat CT indicated further absorption of bilateral lung lesions ( Figure 5 ), The hormone dose was reduced to prednisone 50 mg, and the patient was discharged with a weekly dose reduction of 5-10 mg ( Figure 6 ). As of May 25, 2022, the patient had no restrictions in daily activities, respiratory distress, or other manifestations, and the CT was reviewed in the outpatient clinic ( Figure 7 ). At the follow-up on August 22, 2022, the patient underwent a repeat CT as an outpatient, which showed a visible occupying lesion in the left lung ( Figure 8 ).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 65-year-old man with lung squamous cell carcinoma and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma presented with a 4-day history of fever up to 39 °C, cough with scant white foamy sputum, and progressive dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was diagnosed in September 2021 with left lower lobe bronchial squamous cell carcinoma with liver metastasis and right cervical lymphoid hyperplasia, for which he received four cycles of nab-paclitaxel plus lobaplatin and penpulimab immunotherapy (October–December 2021) followed by maintenance penpulimab (cycles 5–7, January–February 2022). In February 2022, biopsy of newly enlarged FDG-avid left cervical lymph nodes revealed synchronous non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL). He received R-CHOP chemotherapy (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone) on March 18, 2022, and his 8th cycle of penpulimab on March 23, 2022. On March 30, 2022, he developed fever peaking at 39 °C, cough productive of small amounts of white foamy sputum, and dyspnea that failed outpatient cefdinir and ibuprofen, leading to hospital admission on April 3, 2022, and ICU transfer on April 9, 2022, for worsening dyspnea and pulmonary infiltrates.
subjective.past_medical_history: Left lower lobe lung squamous cell carcinoma with liver metastasis (diagnosed September 2021); synchronous non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (diagnosed February 2022); heavy smoking history (smoking index 800: 20 cigarettes/day for 40 years).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high fever (up to 39 °C), cough with scant white foamy sputum, and progressive dyspnea.

objective.physical_examination: Severe cachexia/underweight with BMI 15.2 kg/m2. Upon ICU admission (April 9, 2022): Conscious with intact airway self-purification, severe hypoxemia with SpO2 66%, and tachypnea with respiratory rate 32 breaths/min.
objective.routine_investigations: ICU admission blood gas and laboratory workup: Severe type I respiratory failure with oxygenation index (PaO2/FiO2) of 131 mmHg and cellular immunodeficiency. Microbiological and immunological screening: Negative galactomannan antigen test, negative TORCH panel, negative nucleic acid tests for 9 respiratory pathogens, negative Pneumocystis pneumonia testing, and negative blood and sputum cultures; negative autoimmune antibody panel.
objective.advanced_workup: Pre-NHL PET-CT (mid-January 2022): Strip-like increased density with mild 18F-FDG uptake in the left lower lobe and FDG-avid systemic lymphadenopathy. Admission and ICU chest CT scans (April 3 and April 9, 2022): Progressive diffuse bilateral interstitial pneumonia and extensive pulmonary infiltrates. Fungal biomarker: Elevated serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan at 199.32 pg/mL. Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS): Negative for all pathogenic microorganisms (excluding Pneumocystis jirovecii and other opportunistic infections).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Grade 4 checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis (CIP) complicated by type I respiratory failure, precipitated by sequential R-CHOP (rituximab-mediated B-cell depletion) and penpulimab (anti-PD-1) immunotherapy; severe infectious pneumonia including Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia was ruled out by negative BALF mNGS and negative targeted microbiological assays despite a mildly elevated serum beta-D-glucan (199.32 pg/mL). Plan and clinical course: Managed in the ICU with awake prone noninvasive mechanical ventilation and intravenous methylprednisolone 2 mg/kg/day alongside initial empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics. Clinical symptoms rapidly improved by April 10, 2022, and antibiotics were discontinued once BALF mNGS confirmed no pathogens. Repeat chest CT on April 11 showed lesion absorption; he was weaned from noninvasive ventilation and transferred to the general respiratory ward on April 12. Methylprednisolone was reduced to 40 mg/day on April 15, oxygen was discontinued on April 20 with further CT improvement, and he was discharged on oral prednisone 50 mg/day with a 5–10 mg weekly taper. At follow-up on May 25, 2022, he had normal daily activity without dyspnea, and outpatient CT on August 22, 2022, showed resolution of pneumonitis with a visible left lung mass.
